**Image Analysis:**

The image shows a sugarcane (or sugarcane-family grass) leaf with the following key features:
- **Elongated, longitudinal pale/whitish-yellow streaks** running parallel to the leaf veins
- Alternating pattern of light (pale green to near-white) and dark green areas
- The streaks run continuously along the length of the leaf blade
- No spots, lesions, or necrotic patches visible
- Leaf shape and structure appear otherwise intact (no distortion or curling)

**Differential Reasoning:**

| Class | Match? |
|---|---|
| Brown_Spot | No — no brown circular/oval spots |
| Grassy_Shoot | No — no shoot proliferation |
| Leaf_Scald | Possible, but scald typically shows scalded margins with a distinct pencil-line border |
| Pokkah_Boeng | No — no top leaf distortion or crinkled chlorotic tissue |
| Sett_Rot | No — this is a leaf symptom, not sett/root |
| **Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv** | **Yes — elongated pale streaks running parallel to veins, classic SCSMV appearance** |
| Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus | Possible, but SCMV shows more irregular mosaic blotches, not continuous streaks |
| Yellow_Leaf | No — Yellow Leaf Syndrome shows midrib yellowing, not streaking |
| Yellow_Spot | No — no discrete yellow spots |

The **continuous, elongated pale streaks running lengthwise parallel to the leaf veins** are the hallmark symptom of Sugarcane Streak Mosaic Virus (SCSMV), distinguishing it from the more irregular patchy mosaic of SCMV.
